     1	// HeavyModelAdmission.swift — single-heavy-model residency accounting.
     2	//
     3	// The engine can only afford ONE heavy generative model resident in unified
     4	// memory at a time. A resident image model (krea2 alone footprints ~75GB in
     5	// practice, far above the pool's 22GB estimate) plus LTX-2 video (~60-70GB)
     6	// exceeds a 128GB machine's physical RAM and trips OS_REASON_JETSAM.
     7	//
     8	// The ModelPool's VRAM budget is BLIND to LTX-2 (it loads entirely outside the
     9	// pool), so image + video could co-reside and OOM. This type owns the pure
    10	// accounting decision — "evict the other class, and can this load proceed?" —
    11	// so it is unit-testable with injected byte figures, independent of live
    12	// machine state. WarmServer wires it to MemoryProbe for the live numbers.
    13	//
    14	// Issue: #218
    15	
    16	import Foundation
    17	
    18	/// Which class of heavy model is competing for unified memory.
    19	public enum HeavyModelClass: String, Sendable, Equatable {
    20	  case image
    21	  case video
    22	}
    23	
    24	/// Pure admission-control logic for loading a heavy model into unified memory.
    25	public struct HeavyModelAdmission: Sendable, Equatable {
    26	  /// Physical-RAM headroom to keep free after a heavy load (default 15GB).
    27	  /// Leaving headroom avoids jetsam from transient allocation spikes during
    28	  /// the first denoise/decode pass.
    29	  public let headroomBytes: UInt64
    30	
    31	  public init(headroomBytes: UInt64 = 15 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024) {
    32	    self.headroomBytes = headroomBytes
    33	  }
    34	
    35	  /// Conservative resident-footprint estimate for the LTX-2 video stack
    36	  /// (transformer + connector + VAE + Gemma text encoder), used when deciding
    37	  /// whether an incoming image load must first evict a resident video model.
    38	  public static let ltx2EstimateBytes: UInt64 = 65 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    39	
    40	  /// Estimate for an int8-quantized LTX-2 stack (`ComfyBox quantize-ltx2`
    41	  /// checkpoint + mlx-community int8 Gemma, comfybox#230): video-DiT blocks
    42	  /// 24→12 GB packed, Gemma 24→12.6 GB, plus VAE/embeds and the same
    43	  /// activation headroom the 65 GB bf16 gate implied. Same-seed A/B validated
    44	  /// 2026-07-16 (RMSE ~0.005 vs bf16, render succeeded on the first try).
    45	  public static let ltx2EstimateBytesInt8: UInt64 = 40 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    46	
    47	  /// Precision-keyed LTX-2 estimate: int8 when the weights directory carries
    48	  /// a `quant_manifest.json` (written by `quantize-ltx2`), else the bf16
    49	  /// figure. Keyed off the DIRECTORY so a launch-arg flip back to the bf16
    50	  /// weights restores the conservative gate with no rebuild (FDD §4.3).
    51	  public static func ltx2EstimateBytes(forWeightsPath path: String?) -> UInt64 {
    52	    guard let path, !path.isEmpty else { return ltx2EstimateBytes }
    53	    let manifest = URL(fileURLWithPath: path).appendingPathComponent("quant_manifest.json")
    54	    return FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: manifest.path)
    55	      ? ltx2EstimateBytesInt8 : ltx2EstimateBytes
    56	  }
    57	
    58	  public struct Decision: Sendable, Equatable {
    59	    /// Release the currently-resident models of the *other* class first.
    60	    public let evictOther: Bool
    61	    /// Whether the load may proceed at all.
    62	    public let admit: Bool
    63	    /// Whether headroom will be satisfied (false ⇒ admitted but tight).
    64	    public let hasHeadroom: Bool
    65	    public let reason: String
    66	  }
    67	
    68	  /// Projected free memory once the other heavy class is released.
    69	  /// `availableBytes` already excludes the other class's wired arrays, so
    70	  /// releasing it adds `otherResidentBytes` back to the free pool.
    71	  public func projectedFreeAfterEvict(availableBytes: UInt64, otherResidentBytes: UInt64) -> UInt64 {
    72	    availableBytes &+ otherResidentBytes
    73	  }
    74	
    75	  /// Decide whether a heavy load of `needBytes` may proceed.
    76	  ///
    77	  /// - Parameters:
    78	  ///   - needBytes: estimated footprint of the model we are about to load.
    79	  ///   - availableBytes: reclaimable/free system memory now
    80	  ///     (`MemoryProbe.systemAvailableMemoryBytes()`).
    81	  ///   - otherResidentBytes: estimated footprint of the OTHER heavy class
    82	  ///     currently resident (0 if none). Always evicted first.
    83	  public func decide(needBytes: UInt64, availableBytes: UInt64, otherResidentBytes: UInt64) -> Decision {
    84	    let evict = otherResidentBytes > 0
    85	    let projectedFree = projectedFreeAfterEvict(availableBytes: availableBytes, otherResidentBytes: otherResidentBytes)
    86	
    87	    if projectedFree >= needBytes &+ headroomBytes {
    88	      return Decision(
    89	        evictOther: evict, admit: true, hasHeadroom: true,
    90	        reason: "ok: projected \(projectedFree >> 20)MB free ≥ need \(needBytes >> 20)MB + headroom \(headroomBytes >> 20)MB")
    91	    }
    92	    if projectedFree >= needBytes {
    93	      return Decision(
    94	        evictOther: evict, admit: true, hasHeadroom: false,
    95	        reason: "tight: projected \(projectedFree >> 20)MB free ≥ need \(needBytes >> 20)MB but below headroom target")
    96	    }
    97	    return Decision(
    98	      evictOther: evict, admit: false, hasHeadroom: false,
    99	      reason: "refuse: projected \(projectedFree >> 20)MB free < need \(needBytes >> 20)MB — would OOM")
   100	  }

   855	  // MARK: - Internal: Denoising Loop
   856	
   857	  /// Core denoising loop shared by T2V and I2V.
   858	  private func denoisingLoop(
   859	    latents: MLXArray,
   860	    positions: MLXArray,
   861	    precomputedPE: (cos: MLXArray, sin: MLXArray),
   862	    textEmbeddings: MLXArray,
   863	    negativeEmbeddings: MLXArray?,
   864	    sigmas: [Float],
   865	    cfgScale: Float,
   866	    state: LTX2LatentState?,
   867	    nagEmbeddings: MLXArray? = nil,
   868	    nag: LTX2NAGConfig = .disabled,
   869	    forceDeterministic: Bool = false,
   870	    progressCallback: ((Int, Int) -> Void)?
   871	  ) -> MLXArray {
   872	    let dtype: DType = .bfloat16
   873	    let numSteps = sigmas.count - 1
   874	    // Per-step CFG schedule (community "CFG ramp": e.g. LTX2_CFG_SCHEDULE=3,2,1 —
   875	    // CFG only on the first steps, where broad motion forms, then back to 1;
   876	    // 10Eros per-step guider pattern). Missing entries extend the last value.
   877	    let cfgSchedule: [Float]? = resolvedConfig.cfgSchedule.isEmpty ? nil : resolvedConfig.cfgSchedule
   878	    func cfgAt(_ step: Int) -> Float {
   879	      guard let sch = cfgSchedule else { return cfgScale }
   880	      return sch[min(step, sch.count - 1)]
   881	    }
   882	    let useCFG = (cfgScale > 1.0 || (cfgSchedule?.contains { $0 > 1.0 } ?? false)) && negativeEmbeddings != nil
   883	
   884	    // --- Denoise-trajectory instrumentation (env-gated, off by default) ---
   885	    // Set LTX2_TRAJ_DUMP=<path-prefix> to append one JSON line per step to
   886	    // <path-prefix>.jsonl with latent/x0/velocity statistics. Used to diff
   887	    // sampler behavior numerically against reference implementations
   888	    // (e.g. ComfyUI). Zero overhead when the env var is unset.
   889	    let trajPrefix = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_TRAJ_DUMP"]
   890	    var trajHandle: FileHandle? = nil
   891	    // Mean over all elements.
   892	    func trajMean(_ x: MLXArray) -> MLXArray { x.mean() }
   893	    // Std over all elements (population).
   894	    func trajStd(_ x: MLXArray) -> MLXArray {
   895	      let m = x.mean()
   896	      return MLX.sqrt(((x - m) * (x - m)).mean())
   897	    }
   898	    // Weighted mean/std over token subset. x: (B, T, C) f32, w: (B, T) f32 0/1.
   899	    func trajMaskedStats(_ x: MLXArray, _ w: MLXArray) -> (mean: MLXArray, std: MLXArray) {
   900	      let w3 = w.expandedDimensions(axis: -1)
   901	      let channels = Float(x.dim(-1))
   902	      let count = w.sum() * channels + 1e-6
   903	      let m = (x * w3).sum() / count
   904	      let v = (((x - m) * (x - m)) * w3).sum() / count
   905	      return (m, MLX.sqrt(v))
   906	    }
   907	
   908	    // Keep latents in float32 throughout for precision
   909	    var currentLatents = latents.asType(.float32)
   910	    // Refine pass uses the deterministic member of the sampler family (validated
   911	    // PinkCherry recipe: base=euler_ancestral_cfg_pp, refine=euler_cfg_pp), so
   912	    // forceDeterministic drops the ancestral/SDE noise but keeps CFG++ mode.
   913	    let useSDE = resolvedConfig.samplerIsAncestral && !forceDeterministic
   914	    // CFG++ (euler[_ancestral]_cfg_pp): needs an unconditional (negative) pass
   915	    // every step regardless of cfgScale.
   916	    let useCfgPP = resolvedConfig.samplerIsCfgPP && negativeEmbeddings != nil
   917	
   918	    for i in 0..<numSteps {
   919	      let sigma = sigmas[i]
   920	      let sigmaNext = sigmas[i + 1]
   921	
   922	      // INPUT-side conditioning clamp (matches ComfyUI KSamplerX0Inpaint +
   923	      // LTXV.scale_latent_inpaint which returns the CLEAN latent, never
   924	      // re-noised): conditioned tokens (denoiseMask < 1) enter the model as
   925	      // clean latent every step, consistent with their per-token timestep of
   926	      // ~0. Without this the step update re-mixes noise into conditioned
   927	      // tokens, so the model reads a NOISY frame while told it's clean —
   928	      // misreading the reference each step (appearance divergence, i2v
   929	      // transition pop). Output-side x0 clamping alone is insufficient.
   930	      if let s = state {
   931	        let m = s.denoiseMask.asType(.float32)
   932	        currentLatents = currentLatents * m + s.cleanLatent.asType(currentLatents.dtype) * (MLXArray(Float(1)) - m)
   933	      }
   934	
   935	      // Snapshot pre-step latents for delta_norm (post input-clamp so the
   936	      // delta measures the denoise update; no compute or eval unless
   937	      // trajectory dumping is enabled).
   938	      let trajLatentsBefore: MLXArray? = trajPrefix != nil ? currentLatents : nil
   939	
   940	      let b = currentLatents.dim(0)
   941	      let c = currentLatents.dim(1)
   942	      let f = currentLatents.dim(2)
   943	      let h = currentLatents.dim(3)
   944	      let w = currentLatents.dim(4)
   945	      let numTokens = f * h * w
   946	
   947	      // Flatten latents to token space: (B, C, F, H, W) -> (B, T, C)
   948	      let latentsFlat = currentLatents
   949	        .reshaped(b, c, -1)
   950	        .transposed(0, 2, 1)
   951	        .asType(dtype)
   952	
   953	      // Compute per-token timesteps
   954	      let timesteps: MLXArray
   955	      if let s = state {
   956	        // I2V: per-token timesteps based on denoise mask
   957	        let maskBroadcast = MLX.broadcast(
   958	          s.denoiseMask.reshaped(b, 1, f, 1, 1),
   959	          to: [b, 1, f, h, w]
   960	        )
   961	        let maskFlat = maskBroadcast.reshaped(b, numTokens)
   962	        timesteps = MLXArray(sigma).asType(dtype) * maskFlat.asType(dtype)
   963	      } else {
   964	        timesteps = MLXArray(sigma).reshaped(1, 1).asType(dtype)
   965	      }
   966	
   967	      let sigmaArray = MLXArray([sigma]).asType(dtype)
   968	
   969	      // Positive pass through transformer.
   970	      // Pass PER-TOKEN timesteps so the model sees conditioned frames (mask=0)
   971	      // at timestep 0 (clean) and generated frames at `sigma`. Without this the
   972	      // transformer treats every token as equally noisy and cannot tell which
   973	      // frame is the I2V conditioning frame — it discounts the image and
   974	      // produces T2V-like output. Matches reference guided_denoise_loop which
   975	      // passes `video_timesteps = denoise_mask * sigma` when the mask is
   976	      // non-uniform. For T2V, `timesteps` is a scalar (1,1) → broadcast, so this
   977	      // is a no-op there.
   978	      // NAG rides ONLY the positive pass: it steers the conditional prediction
   979	      // away from the negative concept inside cross-attention. Applying it to
   980	      // the unconditional pass too would guide the baseline that CFG++ steps
   981	      // along, double-counting the guidance.
   982	      let velocityPos = transformer(
   983	        latent: latentsFlat,
   984	        timestep: timesteps,
   985	        context: textEmbeddings.asType(dtype),
   986	        positions: positions,
   987	        sigma: sigmaArray,
   988	        precomputedPE: precomputedPE,
   989	        nagContext: nagEmbeddings?.asType(dtype),
   990	        nag: nag
   991	      )
   992	
   993	      // Compute x0 (denoised) from velocity using per-token timesteps
   994	      let latentsFlatF32 = currentLatents
   995	        .reshaped(b, c, -1)
   996	        .transposed(0, 2, 1)
   997	      let timestepsF32 = timesteps.asType(.float32).expandedDimensions(axis: -1)
   998	      var x0GuidedF32 = latentsFlatF32 - timestepsF32 * velocityPos.asType(.float32)
   999	      let x0CondF32 = x0GuidedF32  // pure conditional x0, saved for the STG delta
  1000	
  1001	      // Negative pass: needed for classic CFG (scale>1) and for CFG++ (every
  1002	      // step, even at cfg=1 — the CFG++ update steps along the UNCONDITIONAL
  1003	      // noise direction; see ComfyUI sample_euler_ancestral_cfg_pp which sets
  1004	      // disable_cfg1_optimization=True for exactly this reason).
  1005	      var x0UncondF32: MLXArray? = nil
  1006	      if useCFG || useCfgPP, let negEmb = negativeEmbeddings {
  1007	        let velocityNeg = transformer(
  1008	          latent: latentsFlat,
  1009	          timestep: timesteps,
  1010	          context: negEmb.asType(dtype),
  1011	          positions: positions,
  1012	          sigma: sigmaArray,
  1013	          precomputedPE: precomputedPE
  1014	        )
  1015	        eval(velocityNeg)
  1016	
  1017	        let x0NegF32 = latentsFlatF32 - timestepsF32 * velocityNeg.asType(.float32)
  1018	        x0UncondF32 = x0NegF32
  1019	        if useCFG && cfgAt(i) > 1.0 {
  1020	          x0GuidedF32 = LTX2Guidance.applyCFG(
  1021	            conditioned: x0GuidedF32,
  1022	            unconditioned: x0NegF32,
  1023	            scale: cfgAt(i)
  1024	          )
  1025	          // Guidance rescale (Lin et al.; counters CFG over-saturation /
  1026	          // shadow-crush). High CFG inflates the prediction's std -> boosted
  1027	          // color/contrast (measured: cfg2 saturation +19% vs seed). Rescale
  1028	          // the guided x0 back toward the CONDITIONAL prediction's std, then
  1029	          // blend by phi — keeps the action-motion boost, restores seed color.
  1030	          // resolvedConfig.guidanceRescale (0 = off) — request/preset capable.
  1031	          let phi = resolvedConfig.guidanceRescale
  1032	          if phi > 0 {
  1033	            let stdCond = MLX.sqrt(((x0CondF32 - x0CondF32.mean()) * (x0CondF32 - x0CondF32.mean())).mean())
  1034	            let stdGuided = MLX.sqrt(((x0GuidedF32 - x0GuidedF32.mean()) * (x0GuidedF32 - x0GuidedF32.mean())).mean())
  1035	            let rescaled = x0GuidedF32 * (stdCond / (stdGuided + 1e-6))
  1036	            x0GuidedF32 = MLXArray(phi) * rescaled + MLXArray(1 - phi) * x0GuidedF32
  1037	          }
  1038	        }
  1039	      }
  1040	
  1041	      // STG: spatiotemporal guidance. A perturbed pass skips self-attention in a
  1042	      // block subset; steer away from it to restore high-frequency motion detail.
  1043	      // For distilled cfg=1 this is the primary guidance lever (anti-haze).
  1044	      let stgBase = resolvedConfig.stgScale
  1045	      if stgBase > 0 {
  1046	        let stgScale = LTX2PipelineConfig.stgScaleForStep(i, base: stgBase)
  1047	        let velocitySTG = transformer(
  1048	          latent: latentsFlat,
  1049	          timestep: timesteps,
  1050	          context: textEmbeddings.asType(dtype),
  1051	          positions: positions,
  1052	          sigma: sigmaArray,
  1053	          precomputedPE: precomputedPE,
  1054	          stgBlocks: resolvedConfig.stgBlockSet
  1055	        )
  1056	        eval(velocitySTG)
  1057	        let x0STGF32 = latentsFlatF32 - timestepsF32 * velocitySTG.asType(.float32)
  1058	        x0GuidedF32 = x0GuidedF32 + MLXArray(stgScale) * (x0CondF32 - x0STGF32)
  1059	      }
  1060	
  1061	      // Reshape x0 from token space to spatial
  1062	      var denoised = x0GuidedF32
  1063	        .transposed(0, 2, 1)
  1064	        .reshaped(b, c, f, h, w)
  1065	
  1066	      // Apply I2V denoise mask
  1067	      if let s = state {
  1068	        denoised = LTX2Conditioning.applyDenoiseMask(
  1069	          denoised: denoised,
  1070	          clean: s.cleanLatent.asType(.float32),
  1230	
  1231	    return currentLatents
  1232	  }
  1233	
  1234	  // MARK: - Internal: Sigma Schedule
  1235	
  1236	  /// Get sigma schedule based on pipeline type.
  1237	  private func getSigmaSchedule(
  1238	    steps: Int, latF: Int, latH: Int, latW: Int
  1239	  ) -> [Float] {
  1240	    switch config.pipelineType {
  1241	    case .distilled:
  1242	      return resolvedConfig.stage1SigmasOrNil ?? LTX2PipelineConfig.stage1Sigmas
  1243	    case .dev, .devTwoStage:
  1244	      let numTokens = latF * latH * latW
  1245	      return LTX2PipelineConfig.devSigmaSchedule(
  1246	        steps: steps,
  1247	        numTokens: numTokens
  1248	      )
  1249	    }
  1250	  }
  1251	
  1252	  // MARK: - Internal: Position Grid
  1253	
  1254	  /// Create a 3D position grid for RoPE in pixel space.
  1255	  ///
  1256	  /// Matches the Python `create_position_grid` function with causal fix
  1257	  /// and bfloat16 precision quantization.
  1258	  /// Adaptive VAE decode. Plain single-pass decode is clean (no spatial-tile
  1259	  /// mosaic, no temporal-window jitter) but memory-heavy; tiled decode is
  1260	  /// OOM-safe for long/large clips. Decide by latent frame count: plain for
  1261	  /// normal clips, exact streamed decode above the safety gate. Mode switch:
  1262	  /// LTX2_DECODE_MODE=auto|stream|tile|plain. Threshold tunable
  1263	  /// via LTX2_PLAIN_DECODE_MAX_LATF (latent frames; ~8x fewer than output frames).
  1264	  private func decodeAdaptive(_ latents: MLXArray) -> MLXArray {
  1265	    let latF = latents.dim(2)
  1266	    let latH = latents.dim(3)
  1267	    let latW = latents.dim(4)
  1268	    // Gate on TOTAL latent volume, not frame count alone: a 768x1280 clip at
  1269	    // latF 13 (24x40 spatial) is 3x the volume of 448x704 and plain decode at
  1270	    // that size drove 40GB+ of swap with critical memory pressure mid-decode,
  1271	    // corrupting the output (blank/gray frames). Budget = the proven-safe
  1272	    // 448x704x97f working point (13*14*22 = 4004) with ~2x headroom.
  1273	    let volume = latF * latH * latW
  1274	    // Default budget derived from the Metal max-buffer ceiling, measured
  1275	    // empirically (2026-07-24): plain-decoding 49f @ 768x1280 (volume 6720,
  1276	    // ~25GB peak intermediate) SILENTLY CORRUPTS the last ~60% of frames —
  1277	    // no error, just garbage — while tiled decode of the same tensor is clean.
  1278	    // 4004 (97f @ 448x704) is proven-safe; 4500 keeps margin below the cliff.
  1279	    let plainMaxVolume = resolvedConfig.plainDecodeMaxVol
  1280	    // LTX2_DUMP_LATENT=<path>: save the pre-decode latent for offline decode
  1281	    // debugging (real-values reproduction harness, #36).
  1282	    if let dumpPath = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_DUMP_LATENT"] {
  1283	      try? MLX.save(arrays: ["latent": latents.asType(.float32)], url: URL(fileURLWithPath: dumpPath))
  1284	      logger.info("VAE decode: dumped pre-decode latent to \(dumpPath)")
  1285	    }
  1286	    // LTX2_DECODE_F32=1: decode in float32 instead of bf16 (debug probe).
  1287	    let decodeF32 = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_DECODE_F32"] == "1"
  1288	    let bf = latents.asType(decodeF32 ? .float32 : .bfloat16)
  1289	
  1290	    // Decode mode — ONE switch (LTX2_DECODE_MODE): auto | stream | tile | plain.
  1291	    //   auto (default): plain under the corruption-safe volume gate, exact
  1292	    //     streamed chunked-io above it (bit-identical to plain, zero seams).
  1293	    //   stream: streamed always. tile: legacy spatial tiling (LTX2_DECODE_TILE).
  1294	    //   plain: force single-pass — EXPERT/DEBUG ONLY: above the gate, MLX Metal
  1295	    //     silently corrupts boundary frames (int32 offset overflow, mlx #3836;
  1296	    //     unfixed in any mlx-swift release as of 0.31.6).
  1297	    // Legacy alias honored: LTX2_DECODE_STREAM=0 -> tile. config.tiledDecode
  1298	    // no longer disables the safety path (Codex review 2026-07-26: a default-
  1299	    // constructed config could force a corrupting plain decode).
  1300	    let env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
  1301	    let mode = (env["LTX2_DECODE_MODE"] ?? (env["LTX2_DECODE_STREAM"] == "0" ? "tile" : "auto")).lowercased()
  1302	    switch mode {
  1303	    case "plain":
  1304	      if volume > plainMaxVolume {
  1305	        logger.warning("VAE decode: FORCED plain above the safety gate (volume \(volume) > \(plainMaxVolume)) — output may be silently corrupt (mlx #3836).")
  1306	      }
  1307	      logger.info("VAE decode: plain single-pass (forced; volume \(volume) [\(latF)x\(latH)x\(latW)]).")
  1308	      return vae.decode(bf)
  1309	    case "tile":
  1310	      let tile = Int(env["LTX2_DECODE_TILE"] ?? "") ?? 16
  1311	      logger.info("VAE decode: tiled (mode=tile; volume \(volume) [\(latF)x\(latH)x\(latW)]) — tile \(tile).")
  1312	      return vae.decodeTiled(bf, tileSize: tile, tileStride: tile - 2)
  1313	    case "stream":
  1314	      logger.info("VAE decode: streamed exact chunked-io (mode=stream; volume \(volume) [\(latF)x\(latH)x\(latW)]) — zero seams.")
  1315	      return vae.decodeStreamed(bf)
  1316	    default:  // auto
  1317	      if volume > plainMaxVolume {
  1318	        logger.info("VAE decode: streamed exact chunked-io (volume \(volume) [\(latF)x\(latH)x\(latW)] > \(plainMaxVolume)) — zero seams.")
  1319	        return vae.decodeStreamed(bf)
  1320	      }
  1321	      logger.info("VAE decode: plain single-pass (volume \(volume) [\(latF)x\(latH)x\(latW)]) — under the safety gate.")
  1322	      return vae.decode(bf)
  1323	    }
  1324	  }
  1325	
  1326	  /// Shared two-stage refine (Phase 3): latent upsample x2 -> re-noise ->
  1327	  /// short refine denoise at high res, with the refine-volume OOM gate and
  1328	  /// optional native-res frame-0 re-anchor. Used by generateI2V AND
  1329	  /// generateMultiKeyframe (continuation chunks) so every chunk of a
  1330	  /// multi-chunk render gets identical refine treatment — previously chunks
  1331	  /// 2+ skipped refine entirely, dropping to base resolution mid-video.
  1332	  /// Returns the refined (or gated/upsampled) latents; caller decodes.
  1333	  private func applyTwoStageRefine(
  1334	    _ latents: MLXArray,
  1335	    latF: Int, latH: Int, latW: Int,
  1336	    textEmbeddings: MLXArray,
  1337	    negativeEmbeddings: MLXArray?,
  1338	    cfgScale: Float,
  1339	    seed: UInt64?,
  1340	    refineAnchorImage: MLXArray?,
  1341	    progressCallback: ((Int, Int) -> Void)?
  1342	  ) -> MLXArray {
  1343	    guard let ups = self.upsampler,
  1344	          resolvedConfig.twoStage else {
  1345	      return latents
  1346	    }
  1347	    logger.info("Two-stage refine: upsampling latents 2x...")
  1348	    // The latent upsampler is trained on UN-normalized (VAE-scale) latents.
  1349	    let stats = vae.decoder.perChannelStatistics
  1350	    let denorm = stats.unNormalize(latents.asType(.float32))
  1351	    let upDenorm = ups(denorm)
  1352	    let upLatent = stats.normalize(upDenorm).asType(.float32)
  1353	    eval(upLatent)
  1354	    // --- Refine bisection instrumentation (env-gated, 2026-08-01 band bug) ---
  1355	    // LTX2_REFINE_ROWSTATS=1 logs per-latent-row energy at each refine boundary
  1356	    // so the vertical-truncation fault can be localized (upsample vs re-noise
  1357	    // vs denoise vs decode) from a single short render.
  1358	    // LTX2_REFINE_DUMP_DIR=<dir> additionally saves the boundary latents as
  1359	    // .npy for offline decode/parity tests.
  1360	    let rowStatsOn = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_REFINE_ROWSTATS"] == "1"
  1361	    let dumpDir = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_REFINE_DUMP_DIR"]
  1362	    func rowStats(_ name: String, _ x: MLXArray) {
  1363	      guard rowStatsOn else { return }
  1364	      let f32 = x.asType(.float32)
  1365	      let energy = MLX.mean(f32 * f32, axes: [0, 1, 2, 4])  // (H,)
  1366	      eval(energy)
  1367	      let rows = energy.asArray(Float.self).map { String(format: "%.4f", $0) }
  1368	      logger.info("REFINE ROWSTATS \(name) [\(x.dim(3)) rows]: \(rows.joined(separator: " "))")
  1369	      if let dir = dumpDir {
  1370	        try? MLX.save(array: f32, url: URL(fileURLWithPath: dir).appendingPathComponent("\(name).npy"))
  1371	      }
  1372	    }
  1373	    rowStats("base", latents)
  1374	    rowStats("upsampled", upLatent)
  1375	    // Refine-volume OOM gate (2026-07-25 23:24 crash): above it, decode the
  1376	    // upsampled latent directly — upscaled-but-unrefined beats a dead server.
  1377	    let refineVolume = upLatent.dim(2) * (latH * 2) * (latW * 2)
  1378	    let refineMaxVolume = resolvedConfig.refineMaxVol
  1379	    if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_REFINE_DECODE_ONLY"] == "1" {
  1380	      logger.info("Two-stage refine: DECODE_ONLY (skipped denoise) — decoding upsampled latent directly.")
  1381	      return upLatent
  1382	    }
  1383	    if refineVolume > refineMaxVolume {
  1384	      logger.info("Two-stage refine: SKIPPED denoise (refine latent volume \(refineVolume) > \(refineMaxVolume)) — decoding upsampled latent directly (OOM guard).")
  1385	      return upLatent
  1386	    }
  1387	    MLX.GPU.clearCache()
  1388	    let rLatH = latH * 2, rLatW = latW * 2
  1389	    let refineSigmas: [Float] = resolvedConfig.refineSigmasEffective
  1390	    if let seed = seed { MLXRandom.seed(seed &+ 1000) }
  1391	    // Flow-matching re-noise: x_σ = (1-σ)·x0 + σ·ε (ComfyUI CONST noise_scaling).
  1392	    let refNoise = MLXRandom.normal(upLatent.shape).asType(.float32)
  1393	    let sigma0 = refineSigmas[0]
  1394	    let mixed = MLXArray(1 - sigma0) * upLatent + refNoise * MLXArray(sigma0)
  1395	    // Frame-0 re-anchor: raw source re-encoded at refine res when available
  1396	    // (workflow nodes 19/20); else the upsampled latent's own frame 0.
  1397	    let rF = upLatent.dim(2)
  1398	    var anchorFrame = upLatent[0..., 0..., 0..<1, 0..., 0...]
  1399	    if var refImg = refineAnchorImage {
  1400	      if refImg.ndim == 4 { refImg = refImg.expandedDimensions(axis: 2) }
  1401	      anchorFrame = vae.encode(refImg).asType(.float32)
  1402	      eval(anchorFrame)
  1403	      logger.info("Two-stage refine: frame 0 re-anchored to source re-encoded at \(rLatW * spatialCompression)x\(rLatH * spatialCompression).")
  1404	    }
  1405	    rowStats("mixed", mixed)
  1406	    let refineInit = MLX.concatenated(
  1407	      [anchorFrame, mixed[0..., 0..., 1..<rF, 0..., 0...]], axis: 2)
  1408	    let refClean = MLX.concatenated(
  1409	      [anchorFrame, upLatent[0..., 0..., 1..<rF, 0..., 0...]], axis: 2)
  1410	    let refMask = MLX.concatenated(
  1411	      [MLXArray.zeros([1, 1, 1, 1, 1]), MLXArray.ones([1, 1, rF - 1, 1, 1])],
  1412	      axis: 2).asType(.float32)
  1413	    let refState = LTX2LatentState(
  1414	      latent: refineInit, cleanLatent: refClean, denoiseMask: refMask)
  1415	    let refinePos = createPositionGrid(batchSize: 1, latF: latF, latH: rLatH, latW: rLatW)
  1416	    let refinePE = ltx2PrecomputeFreqsCIS(
  1417	      indicesGrid: refinePos, dim: innerDim,
  1418	      theta: transformer.positionalEmbeddingTheta,
  1419	      maxPos: transformer.positionalEmbeddingMaxPos,
  1420	      useMiddleIndicesGrid: transformer.useMiddleIndicesGrid,
  1421	      numAttentionHeads: transformer.numHeads,
  1422	      ropeMode: transformer.ropeMode,
  1423	      doublePrecision: transformer.doublePrecisionRoPE)
  1424	    eval(refinePE.cos, refinePE.sin)
  1425	    logger.info("Two-stage refine: denoising at \(rLatW * spatialCompression)x\(rLatH * spatialCompression), \(refineSigmas.count - 1) steps...")
  1426	    // base=euler_ancestral_cfg_pp -> refine=euler_cfg_pp (the author's pairing).
  1427	    var refined = denoisingLoop(
  1428	      latents: refineInit, positions: refinePos, precomputedPE: refinePE,
  1429	      textEmbeddings: textEmbeddings, negativeEmbeddings: negativeEmbeddings,
  1430	      sigmas: refineSigmas, cfgScale: cfgScale, state: refState,
  1431	      forceDeterministic: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_REFINE_DETERMINISTIC"] != "0",
  1432	      progressCallback: progressCallback)
  1433	    eval(refined)
  1434	    rowStats("refined", refined)
  1435	    MLX.GPU.clearCache()
  1436	    logger.info("Two-stage refine complete.")
  1437	    return refined
  1438	  }
  1439	
  1440	  private func createPositionGrid(
  1441	    batchSize: Int,
  1442	    latF: Int,
  1443	    latH: Int,
  1444	    latW: Int,
  1445	    refFrames: Int = 0,   // IC-control: appended reference frames positioned at temporal frame_idx 0

   176	  #if canImport(AVFoundation) && canImport(CoreGraphics)
   177	  /// Write video frames to an MP4 file using AVFoundation.
   178	  ///
   179	  /// Uses H.264 encoding with AVAssetWriter for broad compatibility.
   180	  ///
   181	  /// - Parameters:
   182	  ///   - frames: Array of CGImages to encode.
   183	  ///   - outputPath: Path for the output MP4 file.
   184	  ///   - fps: Frames per second. Default 24.
   185	  ///   - width: Video width in pixels.

   188	  public static func writeMP4(
   189	    frames: [CGImage],
   190	    outputPath: String,
   191	    fps: Int = 24,
   192	    width: Int,
   193	    height: Int,
   194	    bitsPerPixelOverride: Double? = nil
   195	  ) throws {
   196	    guard !frames.isEmpty else {
   197	      throw LTX2PostProcessError.noFrames
   198	    }
   199	
   200	    let outputURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: outputPath)
   201	
   202	    // Remove existing file
   203	    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: outputURL)
   204	
   205	    // Create asset writer
   206	    let writer = try AVAssetWriter(outputURL: outputURL, fileType: .mp4)
   207	
   208	    // Video settings. Bitrate: 0.5 bits/pixel (~12 Mbps @ 768x1280x24) is
   209	    // visually equivalent to the old 4 bits/px for generated content but ~8x
   210	    // smaller — the old setting produced 139MB 12s files that exceeded
   211	    // Telegram's 50MB bot upload cap. Env-tunable via LTX2_VIDEO_BITS_PER_PX.

   213	      ?? Double(ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["LTX2_VIDEO_BITS_PER_PX"] ?? "") ?? 0.5

   215	      AVVideoCodecKey: AVVideoCodecType.h264,
   216	      AVVideoWidthKey: width,
   217	      AVVideoHeightKey: height,
   218	      AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey: [
   219	        AVVideoAverageBitRateKey: Int(Double(width * height * fps) * bitsPerPixel),
   220	        AVVideoMaxKeyFrameIntervalKey: fps,
   221	        AVVideoProfileLevelKey: AVVideoProfileLevelH264HighAutoLevel,
   222	      ] as [String: Any],
   223	    ]
   224

   226	      mediaType: .video,
   227	      outputSettings: videoSettings
   228	    )
   229	    input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
   230	
   231	    let adaptor = AVAssetWriterInputPixelBufferAdaptor(

   233	      sourcePixelBufferAttributes: [
   234	        kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: kCVPixelFormatType_32ARGB,
   235	        kCVPixelBufferWidthKey as String: width,
   236	        kCVPixelBufferHeightKey as String: height,
   237	      ]
   238	    )
   239	
   240	    writer.add(input)
   241	    writer.startWriting()
   242	    writer.startSession(atSourceTime: .zero)
   243	
   244	    let frameDuration = CMTimeMake(value: 1, timescale: Int32(fps))
   245	
   246	    for (index, cgImage) in frames.enumerated() {
   247	      // Wait for input to be ready
   248	      while !input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
   249	        Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.01)
   250	      }

   252	      let presentationTime = CMTimeMultiply(frameDuration, multiplier: Int32(index))
   253

   256	        throw LTX2PostProcessError.pixelBufferCreationFailed(frameIndex: index)
   257	      }

   259	      adaptor.append(pixelBuffer, withPresentationTime: presentationTime)
   260	    }
   261	
   262	    input.markAsFinished()
   263	
   264	    // Wait for writing to complete
   265	    let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
   266	    writer.finishWriting {
   267	      semaphore.signal()
   268	    }
   269	    semaphore.wait()
   270	
   271	    if writer.status == .failed {
   272	      throw LTX2PostProcessError.writingFailed(writer.error?.localizedDescription ?? "unknown")
   273	    }
   274	  }

     2	
     3	Env-gated: set LTX2_TRAJ_DUMP=<path-prefix> before launching ComfyUI.
     4	Monkeypatches comfy.k_diffusion.sampling.to_d — every euler-family sampler
     5	calls it once per step with (x, sigma, denoised) — and appends one JSON line
     6	per step in the same schema as ComfyBox's LTX2_TRAJ_DUMP (qa/video/
     7	trajectory_compare.py consumes both). A sigma increase (schedule restart)
     8	rotates to a new file, so stage-1 and stage-2 refine land in prefix.jsonl /
     9	prefix.2.jsonl just like the Swift side.
    10	
    11	Caveats vs the Swift dump:
    12	- delta_norm here is |x_i - x_{i-1}| observed at step i, i.e. the PREVIOUS
    13	  step's update — one-step offset vs ComfyBox's post-step delta.
    14	- for *_cfg_pp samplers `denoised` is the uncond prediction (that's what
    15	  they feed to_d), so x0_* is approximate for guided runs; exact at cfg 1.0.
    16	
    17	Zero overhead / inert when the env var is unset.
    18	"""
    19	import json
    20	import os
    21	
    22	NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS = {}

    24

    33

    36

    38	    _state = {"fh": None, "last_sigma": None, "prev_x": None, "step": 0, "pass_n": 0}
    39	
    40	    def _rotate():
    41	        _state["pass_n"] += 1
    42	        if _state["fh"]:

    45	        path = _PREFIX + suffix
    46	        _state["fh"] = open(path, "w")
    47	        _state["step"] = 0
    48	        _state["prev_x"] = None
    49	        print(f"[traj_dump] pass {_state['pass_n']} -> {path}")
    50

    52	        d = _orig_to_d(x, sigma, denoised)
    53	        try:

    11	p = {

    16	    "701": {"class_type": "LTXVAudioVAEEncode", "inputs": {

    18	    "702": {"class_type": "LTXVAudioVAEDecode", "inputs": {
    19	        "samples": ["701", 0], "audio_vae": ["196", 0]}},
    20	    "703": {"class_type": "SaveAudio", "inputs": {
    21	        "audio": ["702", 0], "filename_prefix": "audio/ref-roundtrip"}},
    22	}
    23	req = urllib.request.Request(HOST + "/prompt",
    24	    data=json.dumps({"prompt": p, "client_id": "audiotest"}).encode(),
    25	    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    26	try:
    27	    pid = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60))["prompt_id"]
    28	except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    29	    print("REJECTED:", json.loads(e.read()).get("node_errors")); sys.exit(1)
    30	print("queued", pid, flush=True)
    31	for _ in range(180):
    32	    time.sleep(10)
    33	    h = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{HOST}/history/{pid}", timeout=30))
    34	    if pid in h and h[pid].get("status", {}).get("status_str") in ("success", "error"):
    35	        st = h[pid]["status"]
    36	        print("status=", st["status_str"], flush=True)

    41	
    42	**Per-pass distil strength.** HF discussion #8 (tarn1's 1.7-alpha field report) states
    43	the distil LoRA runs at **0.6 on pass 1 and 0.45 on pass 2**. These are per-pass
    44	values, not competing alternatives — an ambiguity that previously led to A/B arms
    45	testing one strength across both passes. Implemented here by giving stage 2 its own
    46	`LoraLoaderModelOnly` + `LTX2_NAG` chain into the stage-2 guider.
    47	
    48	Also from that thread, untested here: the 384 distil reportedly dampens motion and
    49	makes eyes "jumpy"; Kijai's `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-1.1_lora-dynamic_fro09_avg_rank_111_bf16`
    50	is lighter on RAM and reportedly improves movement. An alternative 10-step stage-1
    51	schedule: `1.000, 0.955, 0.893, 0.812, 0.715, 0.603, 0.482, 0.241, 0.121, 0.0`.
    52	
    53	## Deviations from the author, and why
    54	
    55	1. **`VAEDecode` instead of `VAEDecodeTiled`.** The author decodes tiled
    56	   (512/64/4096/8). Todd's instruction is to avoid tiling. Non-tiled decode
    57	   completed without memory trouble at 1280x768 x 121f and at 2560x1536 x 121f.
    58	2. **Audio path removed — forced, not chosen.** LTX-2.3's joint A/V latent path
    59	   produces **black video and silent audio** on ComfyUI 0.29.0 + MPS. Established by
    60	   bisection, not inference:
    61	
    62	   | NAG | Audio | Result |
    63	   |---|---|---|
    64	   | on | on | black |
    65	   | off | on | black |
    66	   | off | off | content |
    67	   | on | off | content |
    68	
    69	   Audio is the sole discriminator; NAG is innocent and is retained. The same fault
    70	   shows up earlier in the chain as `RuntimeError: cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements
    71	   into shape [2, 0, 32, -1]` in `apply_rotary_emb_qk`, reached from
    72	   `comfy/ldm/lightricks/av_model.py`. Consequence: **audio quality cannot be
    73	   validated on Apple silicon** with this stack.
    74	
    75	## Traps that cost time
    76	
    77	- **The latent upscaler must be the official Lightricks file.** ComfyBox's converted
    78	  `spatial_upscaler_x2_v1_1.safetensors` has keys prefixed `spatial_upscaler_x2_v1_1.*`
    79	  and no `__metadata__.config`, so ComfyUI's `LatentUpscaleModelLoader` matches none of
    80	  its branches and fails with `UnboundLocalError: model`.
    81	- **`img_compression` is 22, not 2.** The shipped workflow and any hand-rebuilt graph
    82	  may carry a different value.
    83	- **Core `SaveVideo` cannot mux this audio.** It hands the whole waveform to AAC as one
    84	  frame → `avcodec_send_frame() returned 22`. The author uses VHS_VideoCombine. Save
    85	  audio separately (`SaveAudio`) and mux with ffmpeg, so a late failure cannot discard
    86	  a 20-minute render.
    87	- **v2v: encode at half the target resolution.** Stage 1 runs at half; encoding the
    88	  source at full size overshoots to 2x the intended output (and ~5x the runtime).
    89

   114	## What this says about ComfyBox
   115	
   116	The reference renders **121 frames clean in a single pass**. Our engine's overnight
   117	output (2026-07-31/08-01) corrupts precisely where it chains a continuation chunk:
   118	frames 0-96 clean, chroma blotching from ~frame 100, compounding to the end, on 2 of 2
   119	multi-chunk clips sampled. Both chunks logged `plain single-pass` decode under the
   120	safety gate, so the decoder is not implicated there. Separately, the 241f clip
   121	(`volume 11284 > 4500`, streamed decode) shows a 4-tile mosaic at an interior chunk
   122	boundary while neighbouring frames are fine.
   123	
   124	So the tuning target is the **chaining** — chunk-seed conditioning compression 35,
   125	`strength=1.0` continuation, and the temporal color anchor defaulted OFF since
   126	2026-07-27 — not the model. ComfyBox also emits no audio at all, which is moot for
   127	parity while the reference stack cannot do audio on Metal either.

   131	## 4. Findings from the ComfyUI reference work
   132	
   133	### The author's REAL settings are in his mp4 metadata, not the model card
   134	Every `v1.6/*.mp4` he published embeds the full API graph in the mp4 `comment` tag
   135	(`{"prompt": <api graph>, "workflow": <ui graph>}`). Extract with
   136	`ffprobe -show_entries format_tags=comment`. This is the source of truth — the shipped
   137	workflow JSON and the README differ from what he actually rendered.
   138	
   139	Validated recipe (full detail in `docs/methods/ltx-pinkcherry-comfyui-reference.md`):
   140	- sampler pass1 `euler_ancestral_cfg_pp`, pass2 `euler_cfg_pp`, **CFG 1.0**
   141	- stage-1 sigmas 20-step; stage-2 `0.85, 0.7250, 0.4219, 0.0` (= 3 denoise steps, not 4)
   142	- NAG 11.0 / 0.25 / 2.5
   143	- distil LoRA **384** @ 0.6 (v1.6); **per-pass 0.6 → 0.45** for v1.7 (HF discussion #8)
   144	- **`LTXVPreprocess img_compression: 22`** — we had 2; ComfyBox default is 35
   145	- stage 1 renders at HALF the final size, upsampler x2 brings it back
   146	
   147	### Convention trap: dims mean different things
   148	- **ComfyUI**: the numbers are the FINAL size; stage 1 is internally halved (node 164, x0.5)
   149	- **ComfyBox**: `width`/`height` are the STAGE-1 size; two-stage doubles them
   150	⇒ With two-stage on, the daemon must send HALF dims or every clip is double-size with the
   151	refine silently skipped by `LTX2_REFINE_MAX_VOL` (12000).
   152	
   153	### Divisibility: 32 vs 64
   154	Model requires **/32** (`areValidDimensions`, VAE downsamples by 32). The author's own
   155	`ImageResizeKJv2` uses `divisible_by: 32`. **/64 is only needed because stage 1 runs at
   156	half size and must itself be /32.** All his published dims are /64 (1472x1152, 1408x1024,
   157	960x1280). Frames are always 1+8k (313, 409, 193, 289).
   158

     5	adaln + finale + connector etc. — about ~1.5 GB instead of 22 GB.
     6	
     7	Run from upstream venv:
     8	    cd /Users/dgrauet/sandbox/ltx-reference
     9	    uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/T8_dump_pt_transformer.py
    10	"""
    11	
    12	from __future__ import annotations
    13	
    14	import json
    15	import os
    16	
    17	import numpy as np
    18	import safetensors
    19	import torch
    20	from ltx_core.guidance.perturbations import BatchedPerturbationConfig
    21	from ltx_core.model.transformer.attention import AttentionFunction
    22	from ltx_core.model.transformer.modality import Modality
    23	from ltx_core.model.transformer.model import LTXModel, LTXModelType
    24	from ltx_core.model.transformer.rope import LTXRopeType
    25	
    26	PT_WEIGHTS = os.path.expanduser(
    27	    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Lightricks--LTX-2.3/"
    28	    "snapshots/76730e634e70a28f4e8d51f5e29c08e40e2d8e74/ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors"
    29	)
    30	EMBEDDED_CFG = os.path.expanduser(
    31	    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--dgrauet--ltx-2.3-mlx-q8/"
    32	    "snapshots/03da129baa459c9a70fc5858dee52fa417b3a93d/embedded_config.json"
    33	)
    34	WEIGHT_PREFIX = "model.diffusion_model."
    35	
    36	
    37	def load_weights_for_one_block() -> dict:
    38	    """Load only weights needed for num_layers=1: block 0 + adaln + finale + caption_proj.
    39	
    40	    Strips the 'model.diffusion_model.' prefix to match the model's state_dict keys.
    41	    """
    42	    state: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
    43	    with safetensors.safe_open(PT_WEIGHTS, framework="pt") as f:
    44	        for k in f.keys():  # noqa: SIM118 (safe_open is not a dict)
    45	            if not k.startswith(WEIGHT_PREFIX):
    46	                continue
    47	            new_k = k.removeprefix(WEIGHT_PREFIX)
    48	            # Filter: keep only block 0 + non-block keys
    49	            if "transformer_blocks." in new_k and not new_k.startswith("transformer_blocks.0."):
    50	                continue
    51	            state[new_k] = f.get_tensor(k).to(torch.float32)
    52	    return state
    53	
    54	
    55	def build_model() -> LTXModel:
    56	    with open(EMBEDDED_CFG) as f:
    57	        cfg_full = json.load(f)
    58	    cfg = cfg_full["transformer"]
    59	
    60	    return LTXModel(
    61	        model_type=LTXModelType.AudioVideo,
    62	        num_attention_heads=cfg.get("num_attention_heads", 32),
    63	        attention_head_dim=cfg.get("attention_head_dim", 128),
    64	        in_channels=cfg.get("in_channels", 128),
    65	        out_channels=cfg.get("out_channels", 128),
    66	        num_layers=1,  # ← only 1 block instead of 48
    67	        cross_attention_dim=cfg.get("cross_attention_dim", 4096),
    68	        norm_eps=cfg.get("norm_eps", 1e-06),
    69	        attention_type=AttentionFunction(cfg.get("attention_type", "default")),
    70	        positional_embedding_theta=cfg.get("positional_embedding_theta", 10000.0),
    71	        positional_embedding_max_pos=cfg.get("positional_embedding_max_pos", [20, 2048, 2048]),
    72	        timestep_scale_multiplier=cfg.get("timestep_scale_multiplier", 1000),
    73	        use_middle_indices_grid=cfg.get("use_middle_indices_grid", True),
    74	        audio_num_attention_heads=cfg.get("audio_num_attention_heads", 32),
    75	        audio_attention_head_dim=cfg.get("audio_attention_head_dim", 64),
    76	        audio_in_channels=cfg.get("audio_in_channels", 128),
    77	        audio_out_channels=cfg.get("audio_out_channels", 128),
    78	        audio_cross_attention_dim=cfg.get("audio_cross_attention_dim", 2048),
    79	        audio_positional_embedding_max_pos=cfg.get("audio_positional_embedding_max_pos", [20]),
    80	        av_ca_timestep_scale_multiplier=cfg.get("av_ca_timestep_scale_multiplier", 1),
    81	        rope_type=LTXRopeType(cfg.get("rope_type", "interleaved")),
    82	        double_precision_rope=cfg.get("frequencies_precision", False) == "float64",
    83	        apply_gated_attention=cfg.get("apply_gated_attention", False),
    84	        caption_projection=None,
    85	        audio_caption_projection=None,
    86	        cross_attention_adaln=cfg.get("cross_attention_adaln", False),
    87	    )
    88	
    89	
    90	def make_inputs(seed: int) -> dict:
    91	    """Seeded keyframe-conditioned inputs."""
    92	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    93	    # Tiny shape: F=1, H=2, W=2 -> 4 generation tokens; 2 keyframes appended -> 8 kf tokens
    94	    n_gen, n_kf = 4, 8
    95	    n_total = n_gen + n_kf
    96	
    97	    video_latent = rng.standard_normal((1, n_total, 128)).astype(np.float32)
    98	    audio_latent = rng.standard_normal((1, 4, 128)).astype(np.float32)
    99	    # positions shape (B, num_axes, T, 2) where last dim = [start, end].
   100	    # For midpoint equivalence with MLX scalars, use [start, start+1] so
   101	    # midpoint = start + 0.5. Generate scalar starts and stack [s, s+1].
   102	    video_pos_starts = rng.standard_normal((1, 3, n_total)).astype(np.float32)
   103	    video_pos = np.stack([video_pos_starts, video_pos_starts + 1.0], axis=-1)
   104	    audio_pos_starts = rng.standard_normal((1, 1, 4)).astype(np.float32)
   105	    audio_pos = np.stack([audio_pos_starts, audio_pos_starts + 1.0], axis=-1)
   106	    # Cross-attention text context: (B, 1024 tokens, dim)
   107	    video_ctx = rng.standard_normal((1, 1024, 4096)).astype(np.float32) * 0.1
   108	    audio_ctx = rng.standard_normal((1, 1024, 2048)).astype(np.float32) * 0.1
   109	    sigma = np.array([0.5], dtype=np.float32)
   110	    # Per-token timesteps: gen tokens at sigma, kf tokens at 0 (keyframe-conditioning regime)
   111	    video_ts = np.array([[0.5] * n_gen + [0.0] * n_kf], dtype=np.float32)
   112	    audio_ts = np.array([[0.5] * 4], dtype=np.float32)
   113	    return dict(
   114	        video_latent=video_latent,
   115	        audio_latent=audio_latent,
   116	        video_pos=video_pos,
   117	        audio_pos=audio_pos,
   118	        video_ctx=video_ctx,
   119	        audio_ctx=audio_ctx,
   120	        sigma=sigma,
   121	        video_ts=video_ts,
   122	        audio_ts=audio_ts,
   123	    )
   124	
   125	
   126	def main() -> None:
   127	    print("Building LTXModel(num_layers=1)...")
   128	    model = build_model()
   129	    print("Loading weights (block 0 + adaln + finale)...")
   130	    state = load_weights_for_one_block()
   131	    print(f"  loaded {len(state)} keys")
   132	    missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(state, strict=False)
   133	    print(f"  missing: {len(missing)} unexpected: {len(unexpected)}")
   134	    if missing[:5]:
   135	        print(f"  first missing: {missing[:5]}")
   136	    if unexpected[:5]:
   137	        print(f"  first unexpected: {unexpected[:5]}")
   138	
   139	    model.train(False)
   140	
   141	    inputs = make_inputs(seed=42)
   142	
   143	    video_mod = Modality(
   144	        latent=torch.from_numpy(inputs["video_latent"]),
   145	        sigma=torch.from_numpy(inputs["sigma"]),
   146	        timesteps=torch.from_numpy(inputs["video_ts"]),
   147	        positions=torch.from_numpy(inputs["video_pos"]),
   148	        context=torch.from_numpy(inputs["video_ctx"]),
   149	        enabled=True,
   150	    )
   151	    audio_mod = Modality(
   152	        latent=torch.from_numpy(inputs["audio_latent"]),
   153	        sigma=torch.from_numpy(inputs["sigma"]),
   154	        timesteps=torch.from_numpy(inputs["audio_ts"]),
   155	        positions=torch.from_numpy(inputs["audio_pos"]),
   156	        context=torch.from_numpy(inputs["audio_ctx"]),
   157	        enabled=True,
   158	    )
   159	    perts = BatchedPerturbationConfig.empty(1)
   160	
   161	    print("Running forward...")
   162	    with torch.no_grad():
   163	        vx, ax = model(video_mod, audio_mod, perts)
   164	
   165	    print(f"video out shape: {vx.shape} mean={vx.mean().item():.6f} std={vx.std().item():.6f}")
   166	    print(f"audio out shape: {ax.shape} mean={ax.mean().item():.6f} std={ax.std().item():.6f}")
   167	
   168	    np.savez(
   169	        "/tmp/T8_transformer_pt.npz",
   170	        **inputs,
   171	        video_out=vx.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32),
   172	        audio_out=ax.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32),
   173	    )
   174	    print("wrote /tmp/T8_transformer_pt.npz")
   175	
   176	
   177	if __name__ == "__main__":
   178	    main()
     1	"""T8 (MLX side): LTXModel forward parity, num_layers=1.
     2	
     3	Loads same PT bf16 weights from upstream (model.diffusion_model.* prefix
     4	needs remapping to MLX's transformer.* prefix). Runs forward with same
     5	seeded keyframe-conditioned input, compares against PT dump.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import os
    11	import sys
    12	
    13	import mlx.core as mx
    14	import numpy as np
    15	
    16	from ltx_core_mlx.model.transformer.model import LTXModel, LTXModelConfig
    17	
    18	PT_WEIGHTS = os.path.expanduser(
    19	    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Lightricks--LTX-2.3/"
    20	    "snapshots/76730e634e70a28f4e8d51f5e29c08e40e2d8e74/ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors"
    21	)
    22	MLX_WEIGHTS = os.path.expanduser(
    23	    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--dgrauet--ltx-2.3-mlx/"
    24	    "snapshots/baa5f235ea04fd9c95899d751295c4fd825ee4e2/transformer-dev.safetensors"
    25	)
    26	PT = "/tmp/T8_transformer_pt.npz"
    27	
    28	
    29	def load_mlx_block_0_weights() -> dict:
    30	    """Load only block 0 + adaln + finale weights from MLX bf16 transformer-dev."""
    31	    raw = mx.load(MLX_WEIGHTS)
    32	    out: dict[str, mx.array] = {}
    33	    for k, v in raw.items():
    34	        if not k.startswith("transformer."):
    35	            continue
    36	        new_k = k.removeprefix("transformer.")
    37	        # Filter: keep only block 0 + non-block keys
    38	        if "transformer_blocks." in new_k and not new_k.startswith("transformer_blocks.0."):
    39	            continue
    40	        out[new_k] = v.astype(mx.float32)
    41	    return out
    42	
    43	
    44	def main() -> None:
    45	    pt = dict(np.load(PT))
    46	    cfg = LTXModelConfig(num_layers=1)
    47	    model = LTXModel(cfg)
    48	
    49	    weights = load_mlx_block_0_weights()
    50	    print(f"Loading {len(weights)} MLX weight keys...")
    51	    model.load_weights(list(weights.items()), strict=False)
    52	
    53	    # Build MLX-style inputs from the saved PT inputs.
    54	    # Positions: PT shape (B, 3, T, 2) where last is [start, end]; MLX wants (B, T, num_axes) midpoint.
    55	    video_pos_pt = pt["video_pos"]  # (1, 3, T, 2)
    56	    video_pos_mid = ((video_pos_pt[..., 0] + video_pos_pt[..., 1]) / 2.0).transpose(0, 2, 1)
    57	    audio_pos_pt = pt["audio_pos"]  # (1, 1, T, 2)
    58	    audio_pos_mid = ((audio_pos_pt[..., 0] + audio_pos_pt[..., 1]) / 2.0).transpose(0, 2, 1)
    59	
    60	    video_latent = mx.array(pt["video_latent"])
    61	    audio_latent = mx.array(pt["audio_latent"])
    62	    sigma = mx.array(pt["sigma"])
    63	    video_ts = mx.array(pt["video_ts"])
    64	    audio_ts = mx.array(pt["audio_ts"])
    65	    video_pos = mx.array(video_pos_mid)
    66	    audio_pos = mx.array(audio_pos_mid)
    67	    video_ctx = mx.array(pt["video_ctx"])
    68	    audio_ctx = mx.array(pt["audio_ctx"])
    69	
    70	    print("Running forward...")
    71	    vx, ax = model(
    72	        video_latent=video_latent,
    73	        audio_latent=audio_latent,
    74	        timestep=sigma,
    75	        video_text_embeds=video_ctx,
    76	        audio_text_embeds=audio_ctx,
    77	        video_positions=video_pos,
    78	        audio_positions=audio_pos,
    79	        video_timesteps=video_ts,
    80	        audio_timesteps=audio_ts,
    81	    )
    82	
    83	    vx_np = np.asarray(vx).astype(np.float32)
    84	    ax_np = np.asarray(ax).astype(np.float32)
    85	    print(f"MLX video out shape: {vx_np.shape}")
    86	    print(f"MLX audio out shape: {ax_np.shape}")
    87	
    88	    pt_v, pt_a = pt["video_out"], pt["audio_out"]
    89	    print(f"PT  video out shape: {pt_v.shape}")
    90	    print(f"PT  audio out shape: {pt_a.shape}")
    91	
    92	    if vx_np.shape != pt_v.shape:
    93	        print("FAIL: video shape mismatch")
    94	        sys.exit(1)
    95	    if ax_np.shape != pt_a.shape:
    96	        print("FAIL: audio shape mismatch")
    97	        sys.exit(1)
    98	
    99	    v_delta = float(np.max(np.abs(vx_np - pt_v)))
   100	    a_delta = float(np.max(np.abs(ax_np - pt_a)))
   101	    v_rel = v_delta / max(float(np.max(np.abs(pt_v))), 1e-9)
   102	    a_rel = a_delta / max(float(np.max(np.abs(pt_a))), 1e-9)
   103	    print(f"video max_abs={v_delta:.4e}  rel={v_rel:.4%}")
   104	    print(f"audio max_abs={a_delta:.4e}  rel={a_rel:.4%}")
   105	    print(f"PT  video mean={pt_v.mean():.4f} std={pt_v.std():.4f}")
   106	    print(f"MLX video mean={vx_np.mean():.4f} std={vx_np.std():.4f}")
   107	    print(f"PT  audio mean={pt_a.mean():.4f} std={pt_a.std():.4f}")
   108	    print(f"MLX audio mean={ax_np.mean():.4f} std={ax_np.std():.4f}")
   109	
   110	    fail = max(v_delta, a_delta) > 5e-2
   111	    print()
   112	    print("FAIL" if fail else "OK")
   113	    sys.exit(1 if fail else 0)
   114	
   115	
   116	if __name__ == "__main__":
   117	    main()
     1	# Keyframe parity tests (MLX vs upstream PT)
     2	
     3	Targeted PT-vs-MLX parity tests covering the keyframe pipeline code path,
     4	used to localize the keyframe hold-cut-decay regression to the **VAE
     5	decoder forward** (2026-05-06 investigation).
     6	
     7	## Verdict
     8	
     9	| Test  | Component                              | Result         |
    10	|-------|----------------------------------------|----------------|
    11	| A     | keyframe conditioning code             | bit-exact      |
    12	| B     | sampler step (mask blend, Euler)       | bit-exact      |
    13	| T1    | VAE encoder forward                    | 1 ULP bf16     |
    14	| T2    | AdaLayerNormSingle (uniform + per-token) | a few ULPs fp32 |
    15	| T5    | **VAE decoder forward**                | **DIVERGES (max 0.97, 57% rel)** |
    16	
    17	## How to run
    18	
    19	PT side (in upstream `Lightricks/LTX-2` checkout):
    20	
    21	```bash
    22	cd /Users/dgrauet/sandbox/ltx-reference
    23	uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/dump_pt.py
    24	uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/dump_pt_sampler.py
    25	uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/T1_dump_pt_vae_encoder.py
    26	uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/T2_dump_pt_adaln.py
    27	uv run python /Users/dgrauet/Work/mlx/ports/ltx-2-mlx/tests/parity_keyframe/T5_dump_pt_vae_decoder.py
    28	```
    29	
    30	MLX side (in this repo):
    31	
    32	```bash
    33	uv run python tests/parity_keyframe/check_mlx.py
    34	uv run python tests/parity_keyframe/check_mlx_sampler.py
    35	uv run python tests/parity_keyframe/T1_check_mlx_vae_encoder.py
    36	uv run python tests/parity_keyframe/T2_check_mlx_adaln.py
    37	uv run python tests/parity_keyframe/T5_check_mlx_vae_decoder.py
    38	```
    39	
    40	A/B/T1/T2 print `ALL OK` (max_abs <= 5e-3). T5 prints `FAIL` and a
    41	per-frame divergence table — kept as the diagnostic reference until
    42	the VAE decoder bug is fixed.
    43	
    44	## Weight setup
    45	
    46	PT and MLX share the same bf16 weights from
    47	`dgrauet/ltx-2.3-mlx-q8/vae_{encoder,decoder}.safetensors` and
    48	`dgrauet/ltx-2.3-mlx/transformer-dev.safetensors`. PT side strips the
    49	MLX prefix and transposes Conv3d weights `(O, K_t, K_h, K_w, I)` ->
    50	`(O, I, K_t, K_h, K_w)`. The full upstream
    51	`Lightricks/LTX-2/ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors` is also cached but
    52	unused by these tests (would be needed for a full LTXModel forward
    53	parity, see `T3` placeholder TBD).
    54	
    55	## Per-frame divergence in T5 (current MLX decoder)
    56	
    57	Cumulative temporal error pattern — each frame slightly worse than
    58	the previous, suggesting something in the temporal processing chain
    59	(causal padding, frame-trim after pixel_shuffle_3d, channel
    60	ordering in DepthToSpaceUpsample, or PixelNorm timing).
    61	
    62	```
    63	frame 0: diff=0.014
    64	frame 1: diff=0.001
    65	frame 2: diff=0.016
    66	frame 3: diff=0.025
    67	frame 4: diff=0.035
    68	frame 5: diff=0.035
    69	frame 6: diff=0.048
    70	frame 7: diff=0.049
    71	frame 8: diff=0.048
    72	```
    73	
    74	This explains why T2V works (smooth latents -> per-frame diff
    75	invisible) but keyframe breaks (sharp latent boundary at frame 3->4
    76	amplifies into a visible cut at pixel 24-25).

    12	import MLX
    13	import MLXNN
    14	
    15	/// Bidirectional cross-modal attention for audio-video interaction.
    16	///
    17	/// Phase 3 stub: returns inputs unchanged when audio is nil.
    18	/// Full implementation deferred to Phase 5.
    19	///
    20	/// Architecture (when enabled):
    21	///   A2V: Q from video, K/V from audio -> updates video
    22	///   V2A: Q from audio, K/V from video -> updates audio
    23	///   Each direction has its own AdaLN gating (5 params)
    24	public final class LTX2CrossModalAttention: Module {
    25	
    26	  /// Whether cross-modal attention is structurally enabled.
    27	  /// Even when true, actual computation only happens if audio is non-nil.
    28	  let enabled: Bool
    29	
    30	  public init(enabled: Bool = false) {
    31	    self.enabled = enabled
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  /// Forward pass for cross-modal attention.
    35	  ///
    36	  /// - Parameters:
    37	  ///   - videoHidden: Video hidden states `(B, T_v, dim)`.
    38	  ///   - audioHidden: Audio hidden states `(B, T_a, dim)`, or nil if audio disabled.
    39	  /// - Returns: Updated `(videoHidden, audioHidden)` tuple.
    40	  public func callAsFunction(
    41	    videoHidden: MLXArray,
    42	    audioHidden: MLXArray?
    43	  ) -> (MLXArray, MLXArray?) {
    44	    guard let audio = audioHidden, enabled else {
    45	      return (videoHidden, nil)
    46	    }
    47	    // Full implementation deferred to Phase 5
    48	    return (videoHidden, audio)
    49	  }
    50	}

   564	    def preprocess_text_embeds(self, context, unprocessed=False):
   565	        # LTXv2 fully processed context has dimension of self.caption_channels * 2
   566	        # LTXv2.3 fully processed context has dimension of self.cross_attention_dim + self.audio_cross_attention_dim
   567	        if not unprocessed:
   568	            if context.shape[-1] in (self.cross_attention_dim + self.audio_cross_attention_dim, self.caption_channels * 2):
   569	                return context
   570	        if context.shape[-1] == self.cross_attention_dim + self.audio_cross_attention_dim:
   571	            context_vid = context[:, :, :self.cross_attention_dim]
   572	            context_audio = context[:, :, self.cross_attention_dim:]
   573	        else:
   574	            context_vid = context
   575	            context_audio = context
   576	        if self.caption_proj_before_connector:
   577	            context_vid = self.caption_projection(context_vid)
   578	            context_audio = self.audio_caption_projection(context_audio)
   579	        out_vid = self.video_embeddings_connector(context_vid)[0]
   580	        out_audio = self.audio_embeddings_connector(context_audio)[0]
   581	        return torch.concat((out_vid, out_audio), dim=-1)

   622	    def separate_audio_and_video_latents(self, x, audio_length):
   623	        """Separate audio and video latents from combined input."""
   624	        # vx = x[:, : self.in_channels]
   625	        # ax = x[:, self.in_channels :]
   675	                if frame_mask.numel() > 0 and frame_mask.min() != frame_mask.max():
   676	                    has_spatial_mask = True

   684	        ax, a_latent_coords = self.a_patchifier.patchify(ax)
   685	
   686	        # Inject reference audio for ID-LoRA in-context conditioning
   687	        ref_audio = kwargs.get("ref_audio", None)
   688	        ref_audio_seq_len = 0
   689	        if ref_audio is not None:
   690	            ref_tokens = ref_audio["tokens"].to(dtype=ax.dtype, device=ax.device)
   691	            if ref_tokens.shape[0] < ax.shape[0]:
   692	                ref_tokens = ref_tokens.expand(ax.shape[0], -1, -1)
   693	            ref_audio_seq_len = ref_tokens.shape[1]
   694	            B = ax.shape[0]
   695	
   696	            # Compute negative temporal positions matching ID-LoRA convention:
   697	            # offset by -(end_of_last_token + time_per_latent) so reference ends just before t=0
   698	            p = self.a_patchifier
   699	            tpl = p.hop_length * p.audio_latent_downsample_factor / p.sample_rate
   700	            ref_start = p._get_audio_latent_time_in_sec(0, ref_audio_seq_len, torch.float32, ax.device)
   701	            ref_end = p._get_audio_latent_time_in_sec(1, ref_audio_seq_len + 1, torch.float32, ax.device)
   702	            time_offset = ref_end[-1].item() + tpl
   703	            ref_start = (ref_start - time_offset).unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1).unsqueeze(1)
   704	            ref_end = (ref_end - time_offset).unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1).unsqueeze(1)
   705	            ref_pos = torch.stack([ref_start, ref_end], dim=-1)
   706	
   707	            additional_args["ref_audio_seq_len"] = ref_audio_seq_len
   708	            additional_args["target_audio_seq_len"] = ax.shape[1]

   710	            a_latent_coords = torch.cat([ref_pos.to(a_latent_coords), a_latent_coords], dim=2)
   711	
   712	        ax = self.audio_patchify_proj(ax)
   713	
   714	        # additional_args.update({"av_orig_shape": list(x.shape)})
   715	        return [vx, ax], [v_pixel_coords, a_latent_coords], additional_args
   716	
   717	    def _prepare_timestep(self, timestep, batch_size, hidden_dtype, **kwargs):
   718	        """Prepare timestep embeddings."""
   719	        # TODO: some code reuse is needed here.
   720	        grid_mask = kwargs.get("grid_mask", None)
   721	        if grid_mask is not None:
   722	            timestep = timestep[:, grid_mask]
   723	
   724	        timestep_scaled = timestep * self.timestep_scale_multiplier
   725	
   726	        v_timestep, v_embedded_timestep = self.adaln_single(
   727	            timestep_scaled.flatten(),
   728	            {"resolution": None, "aspect_ratio": None},
   729	            batch_size=batch_size,
   730	            hidden_dtype=hidden_dtype,
   731	        )
   732	
   733	        # Calculate patches_per_frame from orig_shape: [batch, channels, frames, height, width]
   734	        # Video tokens are arranged as (frames * height * width), so patches_per_frame = height * width
   735	        orig_shape = kwargs.get("orig_shape")
   736	        has_spatial_mask = kwargs.get("has_spatial_mask", None)
   737	        v_patches_per_frame = None
   738	        if not has_spatial_mask and orig_shape is not None and len(orig_shape) == 5:
   739	            # orig_shape[3] = height, orig_shape[4] = width (in latent space)
   740	            v_patches_per_frame = orig_shape[3] * orig_shape[4]
   990	        return [vx, ax]
   991	
   992	    def _process_output(self, x, embedded_timestep, keyframe_idxs, **kwargs):
   993	        vx = x[0]
   994	        ax = x[1]
   995	        v_embedded_timestep = embedded_timestep[0]
   996	        a_embedded_timestep = embedded_timestep[1]
   997	
   998	        # Trim reference audio tokens before unpatchification
   999	        ref_audio_seq_len = kwargs.get("ref_audio_seq_len", 0)
  1000	        if ref_audio_seq_len > 0:
  1001	            ax = ax[:, ref_audio_seq_len:]
  1002	            if a_embedded_timestep.shape[1] > 1:
  1003	                a_embedded_timestep = a_embedded_timestep[:, ref_audio_seq_len:]
  1004	
  1005	        # Expand compressed video timestep if needed
  1006	        if isinstance(v_embedded_timestep, CompressedTimestep):
  1007	            v_embedded_timestep = v_embedded_timestep.expand()
  1008	
  1009	        vx = super()._process_output(vx, v_embedded_timestep, keyframe_idxs, **kwargs)
  1010	
  1011	        # Process audio output
  1012	        a_scale_shift_values = (
  1013	            self.audio_scale_shift_table[None, None].to(device=a_embedded_timestep.device, dtype=a_embedded_timestep.dtype)
  1014	            + a_embedded_timestep[:, :, None]
  1015	        )
  1016	        a_shift, a_scale = a_scale_shift_values[:, :, 0], a_scale_shift_values[:, :, 1]
  1017	
  1018	        ax = self.audio_norm_out(ax)
  1019	        ax = ax * (1 + a_scale) + a_shift
  1020	        ax = self.audio_proj_out(ax)
  1021	
  1022	        # Unpatchify audio
  1023	        ax = self.a_patchifier.unpatchify(
  1024	            ax, channels=self.num_audio_channels, freq=self.audio_frequency_bins
  1025	        )
  1026	
  1027	        # Recombine audio and video
  1028	        original_shape = kwargs.get("av_orig_shape")
  1029	        return self.recombine_audio_and_video_latents(vx, ax, original_shape)
  1030	
  1031	    def forward(
  1032	        self,
  1033	        x,
  1034	        timestep,
  1035	        context,
  1036	        attention_mask=None,
  1037	        frame_rate=25,
  1038	        transformer_options={},
  1039	        keyframe_idxs=None,
  1040	        **kwargs,
  1041	    ):
  1042	        """
  1043	        Forward pass for LTXAV model.
  1044	
  1045	        Args:
  1046	            x: Combined audio-video input tensor
  1047	            timestep: Tuple of (video_timestep, audio_timestep) or single timestep
  1048	            context: Context tensor (e.g., text embeddings)
  1049	            attention_mask: Attention mask tensor
  1050	            frame_rate: Frame rate for temporal processing
  1051	            transformer_options: Additional options for transformer blocks
  1052	            keyframe_idxs: Keyframe indices for temporal processing
  1053	            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments including audio_length
  1054	
  1055	        Returns:
  1056	            Combined audio-video output tensor
  1057	        """
  1058	        # Handle timestep format
  1059	        if isinstance(timestep, (tuple, list)) and len(timestep) == 2:
  1060	            v_timestep, a_timestep = timestep
  1061	            kwargs["a_timestep"] = a_timestep
  1062	            timestep = v_timestep
  1063	        else:
  1064	            kwargs["a_timestep"] = timestep
  1065	
  1066	        # Call parent forward method
  1067	        return super().forward(
  1068	            x,
  1069	            timestep,
  1070	            context,
  1071	            attention_mask,
  1072	            frame_rate,
  1073	            transformer_options,
  1074	            keyframe_idxs,
  1075	            **kwargs,
  1076	        )

   131	            ],
   132	        )
   133	
   134	    @classmethod
   135	    def execute(cls, positive, negative, vae, latent, images, strength) -> io.NodeOutput:
   136	        scale_factors = vae.downscale_index_formula
   137	        latent_image = latent["samples"]
   138	        noise_mask = get_noise_mask(latent)
   139	
   140	        _, _, latent_length, latent_height, latent_width = latent_image.shape
   141	
   142	        # Process each image in the batch
   143	        batch_size = images.shape[0]
   144	
   145	        for i in range(batch_size):
   146	            img = images[i:i+1]
   147	
   148	            # Check if image is not black and use batch index as frame index
   149	            if img.max() > 0.001:
   150	                f_idx = i
   151	
   152	                image_1, t = cls.encode(vae, latent_width, latent_height, img, scale_factors)
   153	
   154	                frame_idx, latent_idx = cls.get_latent_index(positive, latent_length, len(image_1), f_idx, scale_factors)
   155	
   156	                if latent_idx + t.shape[2] <= latent_length:
   157	                    positive, negative, latent_image, noise_mask = cls.append_keyframe(
   158	                        positive,
   159	                        negative,
   160	                        frame_idx,
   161	                        latent_image,
   162	                        noise_mask,
   163	                        t,
   164	                        strength,
   165	                        scale_factors,
   166	                    )
   167	
   168	                    # Track this guide for per-reference attention control.
   169	                    pre_filter_count = t.shape[2] * t.shape[3] * t.shape[4]
   170	                    guide_latent_shape = list(t.shape[2:])  # [F, H, W]
   171	                    positive, negative = _append_guide_attention_entry(positive, negative, pre_filter_count, guide_latent_shape, strength=strength)
   172	                else:
   173	                    print(f"Warning: Skipping guide at index {i} - conditioning frames exceed latent sequence length")
   174	
   175	        return io.NodeOutput(positive, negative, {"samples": latent_image, "noise_mask": noise_mask})

   551	def ffn_chunked_forward(self, x):
   552	    if x.shape[1] > self.dim_threshold:
   553	        chunk_size = x.shape[1] // self.num_chunks
   554	        for i in range(self.num_chunks):
   555	            start_idx = i * chunk_size
   556	            end_idx = (i + 1) * chunk_size if i < self.num_chunks - 1 else x.shape[1]
   557	            x[:, start_idx:end_idx] = self.net(x[:, start_idx:end_idx])
   558	        return x
   559	    else:
   560	        return self.net(x)
   561	
   562	class LTXVffnChunkPatch:
   563	    def __init__(self, num_chunks, dim_threshold=4096):
   564	        self.num_chunks = num_chunks
   565	        self.dim_threshold = dim_threshold

    32	public struct LTX2VideoRequest: Sendable {
    33	    public var prompt: String
    34	    public var negativePrompt: String?
    35	    /// nil → text-to-video; a path → image-to-video conditioned on it.
    36	    public var initImagePath: String?
    37	    public var width: Int
    38	    public var height: Int
    39	    /// Frames per chunk; must be 1 + 8k (9, 17, 25, …, 97).
    40	    public var framesPerChunk: Int
    41	    public var steps: Int
    42	    public var seed: UInt64
    43	    /// I2V conditioning strength (0–1).
    44	    public var strength: Float
    45	    /// Conditioning compression (libx264 CRF) override; nil = env/default.
    46	    /// Higher = more motion (frozen-still regime at 0-2), lower = more fidelity.
    47	    public var imgCompression: Int?
    48	    /// CFG guidance override; nil = env/config default. >1 amplifies the
    49	    /// action-prompt direction (primary motion lever, Codex 2026-07-26).
    50	    public var guidance: Float?
    51	    /// Identity re-anchor strength for CONTINUATION chunks (0 = off). Each
    52	    /// continuation chunk conditions on the previous chunk\u{27}s last frame at
    53	    /// frame 0 (hard continuity) AND the ORIGINAL source image at the chunk\u{27}s
    54	    /// last frame at this strength (soft identity pull) \u{2014} counters the
    55	    /// cumulative subject/scene drift of tail-to-head chaining (#219).
    56	    public var identityAnchorStrength: Float
    57	
    58	    /// Frames between mid-pass identity re-anchors for a LONG single/first pass
    59	    /// (0 = off). With only a frame-0 anchor, peripheral subjects (e.g. a
    60	    /// partner's face) drift and melt over a long pass; re-splicing the source
    61	    /// at this interval at `identityAnchorStrength` holds EVERY face. #partnered
    62	    public var identityReAnchorInterval: Int
    63	    /// Target duration; >0 generates continuation chunks (I2V only).
    64	    public var extendToSeconds: Float
    65	    public var fps: Int
    66	    /// Deprecated single-LoRA fields — kept for wire/call-site back-compat.

    68	    public var loraPath: String?
    69	    public var loraStrength: Float
    70	    /// LoRAs merged into the transformer for this render, applied in order.
    71	    public var loras: [LTX2LoRAReference]
    72	    public var outputPath: String

   106	    This layer ensures that the output at time `t` only depends on inputs
   107	    at time `t` and earlier. It achieves this by applying asymmetric padding
   108	    to the time dimension (width) before the convolution.
   109	    """
   110	
   111	    def __init__(
   112	        self,
   113	        in_channels,
   114	        out_channels,
   115	        kernel_size,
   116	        stride=1,
   117	        dilation=1,
   118	        groups=1,
   119	        bias=True,

   125	
   126	        # Ensure kernel_size and dilation are tuples
   127	        kernel_size = nn.modules.utils._pair(kernel_size)
   128	        dilation = nn.modules.utils._pair(dilation)
   129	
   130	        # Calculate padding dimensions
   131	        pad_h = (kernel_size[0] - 1) * dilation[0]
   132	        pad_w = (kernel_size[1] - 1) * dilation[1]
   133	
   134	        # The padding tuple for F.pad is (pad_left, pad_right, pad_top, pad_bottom)
   135	        match self.causality_axis:
   136	            case CausalityAxis.NONE:
   137	                self.padding = (pad_w // 2, pad_w - pad_w // 2, pad_h // 2, pad_h - pad_h // 2)
   138	            case CausalityAxis.WIDTH | CausalityAxis.WIDTH_COMPATIBILITY:
   139	                self.padding = (pad_w, 0, pad_h // 2, pad_h - pad_h // 2)
   140	            case CausalityAxis.HEIGHT:
   141	                self.padding = (pad_w // 2, pad_w - pad_w // 2, pad_h, 0)
   142	            case _:
   143	                raise ValueError(f"Invalid causality_axis: {causality_axis}")
   144	
   145	        # The internal convolution layer uses no padding, as we handle it manually
   146	        self.conv = ops.Conv2d(

   213	class Upsample(nn.Module):
   214	    def __init__(self, in_channels, with_conv, causality_axis: CausalityAxis = CausalityAxis.HEIGHT):
   215	        super().__init__()
   216	        self.with_conv = with_conv
   217	        self.causality_axis = causality_axis
   218	        if self.with_conv:
   219	            self.conv = make_conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, kernel_size=3, stride=1, causality_axis=causality_axis)
   220	
   221	    def forward(self, x):
   222	        x = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(x, scale_factor=2.0, mode="nearest")
   223	        if self.with_conv:
   224	            x = self.conv(x)
   225	            # Drop FIRST element in the causal axis to undo encoder's padding, while keeping the length 1 + 2 * n.
   226	            # For example, if the input is [0, 1, 2], after interpolation, the output is [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2].
   227	            # The causal convolution will pad the first element as [-, -, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2],
   228	            # So the output elements rely on the following windows:
   229	            # 0: [-,-,0]
   230	            # 1: [-,0,0]
   231	            # 2: [0,0,1]
   232	            # 3: [0,1,1]
   233	            # 4: [1,1,2]
   234	            # 5: [1,2,2]
   235	            # Notice that the first and second elements in the output rely only on the first element in the input,
   236	            # while all other elements rely on two elements in the input.
   237	            # So we can drop the first element to undo the padding (rather than the last element).
   238	            # This is a no-op for non-causal convolutions.
   239	            match self.causality_axis:
   240	                case CausalityAxis.NONE:
   241	                    pass  # x remains unchanged
   242	                case CausalityAxis.HEIGHT:
   243	                    x = x[:, :, 1:, :]
   244	                case CausalityAxis.WIDTH:
   245	                    x = x[:, :, :, 1:]
   246	                case CausalityAxis.WIDTH_COMPATIBILITY:
   247	                    pass  # x remains unchanged
   248	                case _:
   249	                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid causality_axis: {self.causality_axis}")
   250	
   251	        return x
